songs.mood: C major, purely diatonic, bright square chords under a high lead: the cheerful start.
E major with a light mixolydian ♭7, two independent melodies over pads: friendly, adventurous.
G major, stately bass walk G–F#–E–B, running arpeggio: orchestral NES.
A♭ major with a lydian ♯4, the densest track (10.6 notes per beat): soaring optimism.
C# minor, two channels of continuous arpeggios echoing each other: mechanical, layered.
B♭ minor, an unbroken sixteenth-note line over pads, ♭2 and ♯4 colour: obsessive.
E♭ with a minor tonic chord (E♭m), driving at 144 bpm and the most chromatic track: intense; minor, so dorian rather than mixolydian.
E minor, the bass walks down chromatically (E D C B … B♭ A♭ F#): anxious.
G minor grinding a ♭2 over a pedal, busy drums: complex, tense.
B minor, a moving bass line and dense drums under sparse pads: restless.
E minor (the importer's reading; the profile alone says G minor): a bass sliding E–E♭–D–C, ominous and unstable.
D minor with ♭2 and chromatic turns at 72 bpm: uneasy; its ♭2 suits phrygian.
B♭ minor, one bass note every four bars, 1.6 notes per beat: cold and minimal.
D minor, sparse, purely modal (no chromatic notes): solemn, existential.
